sessions.name: A
sessions.reply:
The costs are now in a new `groceries.csv` (columns `item,cost_usd`), and `meal-plan.md` has no prices left. I searched it for `$`, "usd", "cost" and "price" and found no matches.

- **groceries.csv:** it has one row per dinner, using the same per-dinner estimates as before. They add up to $63, but I didn't add a total row, to keep the file to just those two columns.
- **meal-plan.md:** I removed the cost column, the total, the range and the note about `budget.csv`. I also dropped the price assumption line, since it was about costs. The dinners, shopping list and Thanksgiving note are unchanged.

I can't save this rule for future sessions on my own. If you want it applied automatically in this workspace, say so and I'll add it to a `CLAUDE.md`.

sessions.name: B
sessions.reply:
I wrote the plan to `meal-plan.md`, and the dinners come to about $75, well under your $200.

I used the dinners and costs already in `groceries.csv`, which cover Mon 11/23 to Sun 11/29. Those costs look like they're for two people, so I doubled Saturday's pork stir-fry from $12 to $24 for four.

- **Dinners:** Monday to Friday plus Sunday cost $51 ($11, $8, $7, $8, $10, $7), and Saturday is $24.
- **Left over:** $125 of the $200 remains for breakfasts, lunches, snacks and drinks.
- **Not checked:** I only have costs for dinners. `budget.csv` has no grocery line, so I couldn't check the $200 against anything else. If breakfasts, lunches and extras for the weekend come to more than $125, you'd go over.
- **Assumption:** I assumed the CSV costs are for two people. If they're really for four, the dinner total would be lower.
